result.summary: Adds an optional build-time script evaluation tracer exposed via the libbitcoinkernel C API and its C++ wrapper. When compiled with `-DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON`, macro hooks in `EvalScript` dispatch execution state frames (begin, step, end) to a registered global callback on every opcode evaluation. In non-tracing builds, the hooks compile to no-op stubs with zero runtime overhead.
result.problem: External applications using libbitcoinkernel cannot inspect intermediate script execution state step-by-step, making it impossible to build script debuggers or fine-grained execution analyzers on top of the library. In addition, interpreter unit tests and fuzzing cannot easily observe whether intermediate script states are correct before a subsequent error condition shadows faulty behavior.
evidence: The PR author implemented a proof-of-concept debugger targeting rust-bitcoinkernel demonstrating the trace API in practice (PR description).
The author cites PR #33961 as an example where script interpreter bugs were obscured because unexpected behavior was shadowed by a later error condition (PR description).
result.scope_notes: Touches core consensus validation code in `src/script/interpreter.cpp` by inserting `SCRIPT_TRACE_SCOPE` and `SCRIPT_TRACE_STEP` macro invocations into `EvalScript`. By default, `ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE` is turned off and the macros evaluate to `static_assert(true)`.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the implementation architecture or scope; the patch remains a single commit introducing the CMake option, interpreter trace macros, C/C++ bitcoinkernel wrapper APIs, and unit tests.
result.card: Adds an optional build-time script evaluation tracer exposed through the libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper. External consumers currently cannot inspect intermediate interpreter execution steps to construct script debuggers or execution analyzers. The author implemented a proof-of-concept debugger using rust-bitcoinkernel to demonstrate the interface, and highlights potential testing and fuzzing benefits to prevent errors from shadowing interpreter defects. The feature is disabled by default via CMake and requires no prerequisite PRs.

risk.why: A mistake in the macro hooks or control flow inside EvalScript could alter script evaluation behavior or break the build across compilers.
